reference_sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_customers
FROM (
  -- one row per registered customer
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n_orders
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
) AS t
WHERE t.n_orders >= 2
alternatives:
WITH customer_orders AS (
  -- one row per registered customer
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n_orders
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_customers
FROM customer_orders
WHERE n_orders >= 2

SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_customers
FROM (
  -- one row per registered customer with two or more orders
  SELECT customer_id
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
) AS t

other_way.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_customers
FROM (
  -- one row per registered customer with two or more orders
  SELECT customer_id
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
) AS t
other_way.tradeoff: HAVING inside the derived table filters the customers there; the outer WHERE keeps the order count as a column you can check.
